text_en: Many mothers experience changing emotions in the days after birth. Feeling tearful or low can occur during early adjustment, but feelings that become intense, worsen, or continue beyond about two weeks deserve attention from a health worker.
text_rw: Ababyeyi benshi bagira ibyiyumvo bihindagurika mu minsi ikurikira kubyara. Kurira cyangwa kumva ubabaye bishobora kubaho mu ntangiriro, ariko iyo ibyo byiyumvo bikomeye, birushaho kuba bibi, cyangwa bikomeza ibyumweru birenga bibiri, ni ngombwa kuvugana n’umukozi w’ubuzima.
queries_en: baby blues emotional changes tearful crying low mood after birth two weeks
queries_rw: agahinda nyuma yo kubyara kurira ibyiyumvo bihindagurika ibyumweru bibiri

text_en: Persistent sadness, hopelessness, loss of interest, or difficulty functioning after childbirth can be signs that a mother needs mental-health support. These problems are treatable, and asking a trained health worker for help is an appropriate next step.
text_rw: Agahinda gakomeza, kubura icyizere, kutishimira ibintu, cyangwa kunanirwa gukora imirimo nyuma yo kubyara bishobora kugaragaza ko umubyeyi akeneye ubufasha bwo mu mutwe. Ibi bibazo biravurwa, kandi gusaba ubufasha umukozi w’ubuzima wabihuguriwe ni intambwe nziza.
queries_en: depressed hopeless miserable numb no interest cannot function worthless
queries_rw: numva mfite agahinda nyuma yo kubyara kwiheba kubura icyizere agahinda gakabije nta byishimo nta cyo maze

text_en: Strong anxiety after birth may feel like constant worry, fear, panic, or being unable to relax. A mother who feels extremely anxious should seek advice from a health worker; postpartum anxiety is common and professional support can help.
text_rw: Guhangayika cyane nyuma yo kubyara bishobora kugaragara nko guhora ufite impungenge, ubwoba, igihunga, cyangwa kutabasha gutuza. Umubyeyi uhangayitse cyane akwiriye kugisha inama umukozi w’ubuzima; ubufasha bw’umwuga bushobora kumufasha.
queries_en: anxious worry worried fear scared panic racing thoughts cannot relax
queries_rw: guhangayika impungenge ubwoba igihunga sinshobora gutuza

source: WHO Perinatal Mental Health Integration Guide
text_en: Feeling overwhelmed does not mean that a mother is failing. Support can include listening without judgement, helping her identify immediate needs, reducing practical burdens, and connecting her with family, community, or health services.
text_rw: Kumva ibintu bikurenze ntibivuze ko wananiwe kuba umubyeyi. Ubufasha bushobora kuba ukumva nta kugucira urubanza, kumenya ibyo ukeneye ubu, kugabanya imirimo ikuremereye, no kuguhuza n’umuryango, abaturage, cyangwa serivisi z’ubuzima.
queries_en: overwhelmed too much cannot cope failing mother everything on top of me
queries_rw: byandenze sinshoboye kunanirwa kuba umubyeyi ibintu byinshi

text_en: Fatigue is common after childbirth, but severe exhaustion and ongoing sleep difficulty can also accompany emotional distress. Rest when possible, ask trusted people for practical help, and speak with a health worker when exhaustion is persistent or affects daily functioning.
text_rw: Umunaniro urasanzwe nyuma yo kubyara, ariko kunanirwa cyane no gukomeza kubura ibitotsi bishobora no kujyana n’ihungabana ry’ibyiyumvo. Ruhuka igihe bishoboka, saba abo wizeye kugufasha, kandi uvugane n’umukozi w’ubuzima niba umunaniro ukomeza cyangwa ukubangamira mu buzima bwa buri munsi.
queries_en: cannot sleep insomnia exhausted tired no energy awake all night fatigue
queries_rw: sinshobora gusinzira kubura ibitotsi umunaniro ndananiwe nta mbaraga

source: WHO Perinatal Mental Health Integration Guide
text_en: Guilt, harsh self-blame, or feeling like a bad mother can be part of postpartum emotional distress. A supportive response acknowledges the difficulty, avoids judgement, and encourages the mother to share these feelings with someone she trusts or a trained health worker.
text_rw: Kumva ufite icyaha, kwigaya cyane, cyangwa kumva uri umubyeyi mubi bishobora kujyana n’ihungabana nyuma yo kubyara. Ni byiza kwemera ko bikugoye uticira urubanza, ukabiganiriza umuntu wizeye cyangwa umukozi w’ubuzima wabihuguriwe.
queries_en: guilty blame myself bad mother failure worthless not good enough
queries_rw: numva mfite icyaha ndigaya ndi umubyeyi mubi nta cyo maze

text_en: Practical and emotional support can protect a mother’s wellbeing after birth. She may ask a partner, relative, friend, community health worker, nurse, or peer group for specific help such as listening, preparing food, household tasks, or time to rest.
text_rw: Ubufasha mu mirimo no mu byiyumvo bushobora kurinda imibereho myiza y’umubyeyi nyuma yo kubyara. Ashobora gusaba uwo bashakanye, uwo mu muryango, inshuti, umujyanama w’ubuzima, umuforomo, cyangwa itsinda ry’ababyeyi kumutega amatwi, gutegura ibiryo, gukora imirimo, cyangwa kumuha igihe cyo kuruhuka.
queries_en: alone lonely no support nobody helps partner family friends isolated
queries_rw: ndi jyenyine nta mfashanyo umuryango inshuti uwo twashakanye irungu

text_en: Partners and family members can support postpartum wellbeing by listening, sharing caregiving and household work, attending postnatal contacts, and taking a mother’s emotional concerns seriously. Persistent conflict, threats, or violence require additional professional and safety support.
text_rw: Abo bashakanye n’umuryango bashobora gufasha umubyeyi bamwumva, bagabana kwita ku mwana n’imirimo yo mu rugo, bakajyana na we kwa muganga, kandi bagafata ibyiyumvo bye nk’ibikomeye. Amakimbirane akomeza, iterabwoba, cyangwa ihohoterwa bisaba ubufasha bw’umwuga n’ubw’umutekano.
queries_en: husband partner relationship family conflict ignored no help violence abuse
queries_rw: umugabo uwo twashakanye umuryango amakimbirane kunyirengagiza ihohoterwa

text_en: Stillbirth, miscarriage, or the death or serious illness of a baby can bring profound grief. Compassionate care should respect the mother’s way of grieving and connect her with trusted people, bereavement support, and trained health workers when needed.
text_rw: Gupfusha umwana, gukuramo inda, cyangwa kugira umwana urwaye cyane bishobora gutera agahinda gakomeye. Ubufasha bwuje impuhwe bugomba kubaha uburyo umubyeyi agaragaza agahinda no kumuhuza n’abantu yizeye, abafasha abapfushije, n’abakozi b’ubuzima igihe bikenewe.
queries_en: miscarriage stillbirth baby died loss grief bereavement mourning
queries_rw: gupfusha umwana gukuramo inda agahinda ikiriyo urupfu rw'umwana

text_en: Emotional distress can make bonding or daily care feel difficult. This does not make someone a bad mother. Gentle support for the mother’s mental health can also support her relationship with the baby; persistent difficulty should be discussed with a health worker.
text_rw: Ihungabana ry’ibyiyumvo rishobora gutuma kwegera umwana cyangwa kumwitaho buri munsi bigorana. Ibi ntibivuze ko uri umubyeyi mubi. Gufasha ubuzima bwo mu mutwe bw’umubyeyi bishobora no gufasha umubano we n’umwana; iyo bikomeje, biganirize umukozi w’ubuzima.
queries_en: cannot bond disconnected from baby no love distant bad mother attachment
queries_rw: sinshobora kwegera umwana sinumva mukunda nitandukanyije n'umwana

text_en: Irritability and anger can accompany exhaustion, anxiety, or depression after birth. Step away briefly when the baby is safe, ask someone trusted to help, and discuss persistent or frightening anger with a health worker.
text_rw: Kurakara no kugira umujinya bishobora kujyana n’umunaniro, guhangayika, cyangwa kwiheba nyuma yo kubyara. Niba umwana atekanye, fata akanya gato, saba umuntu wizeye kugufasha, kandi ubwire umukozi w’ubuzima niba umujinya ukomeza cyangwa ugutera ubwoba.
queries_en: angry irritable rage frustrated losing temper shouting

text_en: Difficulty eating, bathing, concentrating, making decisions, or completing basic daily activities can signal significant postpartum distress. A mother experiencing these changes should receive practical support and assessment from a trained health worker.
text_rw: Kunanirwa kurya, kwiyuhagira, kwibanda ku kintu, gufata ibyemezo, cyangwa gukora imirimo y’ibanze bishobora kugaragaza ihungabana rikomeye nyuma yo kubyara. Umubyeyi ufite ibi bimenyetso akwiriye gufashwa mu mirimo no gusuzumwa n’umukozi w’ubuzima wabihuguriwe.
queries_en: cannot eat cannot shower cannot concentrate decisions daily tasks no appetite
queries_rw: sinshobora kurya kwiyuhagira kwibanda gufata ibyemezo gukora imirimo

text_en: Postnatal care should include assessment of the mother’s mood and screening for depression or anxiety, with referral and management when needed. A mother can bring emotional concerns to a nurse, midwife, community health worker, counsellor, or doctor even if she is unsure how serious they are.
text_rw: Kwita ku mubyeyi nyuma yo kubyara bigomba kubamo kubaza uko yiyumva no gusuzuma kwiheba cyangwa guhangayika, hanyuma agahabwa ubufasha bukwiye. Umubyeyi ashobora kubwira umuforomo, umubyaza, umujyanama w’ubuzima, umujyanama mu by’imitekerereze, cyangwa umuganga nubwo yaba atazi neza uburemere bw’ikibazo.
queries_en: need help therapist counsellor doctor nurse health worker treatment screening
queries_rw: nkeneye ubufasha umuganga umuforomo umujyanama w'ubuzima gusuzumwa

text_en: Sudden hallucinations, fixed false beliefs, severe confusion, or rapidly changing extreme mood after childbirth may indicate postpartum psychosis. This is a medical emergency: the mother should not be left alone and needs urgent professional care.
text_rw: Kubona cyangwa kumva ibintu bitariho, kwizera ibintu bitari ukuri, urujijo rukomeye, cyangwa ibyiyumvo bikabije bihinduka vuba nyuma yo kubyara bishobora kuba uburwayi bukomeye bwo mu mutwe. Ni ikibazo cyihutirwa: umubyeyi ntagomba gusigara wenyine kandi akeneye ubufasha bw’umuganga ako kanya.
queries_en: hearing voices seeing things hallucinations delusions confused psychosis mania emergency
queries_rw: kumva amajwi kubona ibitariho urujijo uburwayi bwo mu mutwe byihutirwa
